I am a woman of 41 years, farming alone on my small piece of land here in Balaka. My plot is not even one hectare, so I must be careful with every kwacha I spend. Last season the rains were not so good here in the south, so I am worried about spending too much on fertilizer. I will try to get the subsidy coupon for one bag of NPK and one bag of urea if my name is on the list — if not, I will only buy what little I can afford, maybe half a bag, and I will put the manure from my goats on the rest. I will plant the improved maize seed because my neighbor got better cobs last year with it, but I cannot afford pesticide, and there is no river close by for watering.
